from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite & Intuition: The 'Language' of Coordinates", [
            "A basis acts as your coordinate system's grid. [Asset: grid_01]",
            "Standard vectors i and j define your directions. [Asset: vectors_01]",
            "Point (3, 2) is a simple set of instructions. [Asset: point_01]"
        ])
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 4, 1], y_range=[-1, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        # Fix: Axes object does not have get_grid. Use get_grid method from NumberPlane or simply define the grid lines manually if needed.
        # Alternatively, using get_grid is not an Axes method; NumberPlane is the grid-based class.
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-1, 4, 1], y_range=[-1, 4, 1]).scale(0.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(grid, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(grid))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        e1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(1, 0), color="#FF0000")
        e2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(0, 1), color="#FF0000")
        basis = VGroup(e1, e2)
        
        # Anchor basis to center of axes which is at grid['B2' to 'E5']
        basis.move_to(grid.get_center())
        
        self.play(Create(basis))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(3, 2), color="#00FF00")
        dashed_x = DashedLine(axes.c2p(3, 0), axes.c2p(3, 2), color="#FFFF00")
        dashed_y = DashedLine(axes.c2p(0, 2), axes.c2p(3, 2), color="#FFFF00")
        
        # Attach to the grid group
        point.move_to(grid.c2p(3, 2))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(point))
        self.play(Create(dashed_x), Create(dashed_y))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(dashed_x), FadeOut(dashed_y), FadeOut(grid), FadeOut(basis), FadeOut(point))

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Problem: Changing Perspectives", [
            "Now introduce a new, tilted basis system.",
            "The point remains stationary in space.",
            "Coordinates change to describe the same location."
        ])
        
        # Define Basis 1 (Standard)
        basis1 = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        vec1 = Vector([1, 1], color="#00FFFF")
        group1 = VGroup(basis1, vec1)
        
        # Define Basis 2 (Tilted)
        basis2 = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).rotate(45*DEGREES).scale(0.5)
        vec2 = Vector([1, 1], color="#FF00FF").rotate(45*DEGREES)
        group2 = VGroup(basis2, vec2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_in_area(group1, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(group1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        # Keep point stationary, just highlight the vector
        self.play(Indicate(vec1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Show transformation to tilted basis
        self.play(Transform(group1, group2))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Transition matrix P translates between bases.",
            "Columns of P are new basis vectors.",
            "Apply [v]_old = P * [v]_new for conversion.",
            "Visualize the mapping process.",
            "Example: P = [[1, -1], [1, 1]] maps coordinates."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mechanism: The Transition Matrix (P)", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show matrix P
        matrix_p = MathTex("P = \\begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\\\ 1 & 1 \\end{pmatrix}")
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_p))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Columns of P are new basis vectors
        col1 = matrix_p[0][6:10] # Simplified selection
        col2 = matrix_p[0][10:14]
        self.play(col1.animate.set_color("#00FF00"), col2.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Apply [v]_old = P * [v]_new
        equation = MathTex("[v]_{old} = P \\cdot [v]_{new}")
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "D2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Visualize the mapping process
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_at_grid(axes, "E4", scale_factor=0.4)
        dot = Dot(color=RED).move_to(axes.c2p(1, 1))
        self.play(Create(axes), FadeIn(dot))
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Example P
        example = Text("P maps basis vectors.", font_size=20, color=ORANGE)
        self.place_at_grid(example, "F2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(example))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(ORANGE)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Basis is just a coordinate system choice.",
            "Transition matrices act as system translators.",
            "Perspective changes, but the space remains invariant."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Reflection", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        recap_label = Text("Changing Perspectives", color=YELLOW)
        transition_matrix = MathTex("P", color=RED).scale(2)
        coord_map = VGroup(
            Dot(color=BLUE),
            Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=WHITE)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(recap_label, 'B2')
        self.play(FadeIn(recap_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))
        self.place_at_grid(transition_matrix, 'D3')
        self.play(FadeIn(transition_matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.place_at_grid(coord_map, 'E3')
        self.play(FadeIn(coord_map))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in Mathematics or Engineering

sections.title: Prerequisite & Intuition: The 'Language' of Coordinates
sections.content: Define a basis as a coordinate system (a set of grid lines). Visualize the standard basis (x, y) as a square grid. Explain that a point (3, 2) is just a set of instructions: '3 steps along the red vector, 2 steps along the blue vector'.
sections.example: Imagine a character 'Pixel' living on a standard grid. The basis vectors {i, j} are his compass directions North and East.

sections.title: The Problem: Changing Perspectives
sections.content: Introduce a new 'tilted' basis. Show how the same point in space now needs different numbers to be described. Emphasize that the point hasn't moved, but our perspective has shifted.
sections.example: Pixel wears 'Magic Goggles' that tilt his world by 45 degrees. To him, the same stationary tree now looks like it's at different coordinate values.

sections.title: The Mechanism: The Transition Matrix (P)
sections.content: Formally derive the transition matrix P, where columns are the new basis vectors expressed in terms of the old basis. Equation: [v]_old = P * [v]_new. Use animation to show the mapping process.
sections.example: If the new basis vectors are {1,1} and {-1,1}, demonstrate how to build matrix P = [[1, -1], [1, 1]] to transform old coordinates to new ones.

sections.title: Application: Why Do We Care?
sections.content: Explain that we choose bases to make calculations easier (e.g., diagonalization). Use a visual of a complex shape that looks complicated in standard basis but becomes a simple rectangle in a 'smarter' basis.
sections.example: A robot arm (the device) calculating joint angles. It’s easier to describe the 'hand' position relative to the 'shoulder' (local basis) rather than the 'room' origin (global basis).

sections.title: Summary & Reflection
sections.content: Recap: (1) Basis = coordinate system, (2) Transition Matrix = translator between systems. Remind students: The space is invariant; only the description changes.
sections.example: Final shot: A map of a park. The map stays the same, but you can describe a treasure’s location starting from the 'Front Gate' or the 'Old Oak Tree'. Both are correct; one might just be easier for the treasure hunter.

[VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The point animation is placed too close to the vector lines, leading to visual overlap and ambiguity. Fix: self.place_at_grid(point_01, 'D4', scale_factor=0.5) (line=3, object=point_01)

[VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: Coordinate text overlaps with the lower boundary of the animation frame, reducing legibility. Fix: Line 3: self.place_at_grid(new_coords_01, 'F3', scale_factor=0.5) (line=3, object=new_coords_01)

[VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Axes object is placed too low (E4), causing it to clip near the bottom edge of the frame. Fix: Line 81: self.place_in_area(axes, 'B4', 'D6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=81, object=axes)
